findings.title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
findings.comment:

Allergen Awareness information (given during the previous inspection) is in black binder with the other paperwork. Certified Food Protection Managers are required to obtain allergen awareness training in Class I facilities. Certificates must be renewed every 3 years.

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
-Heavy cream observed in the bar cooler without any date-marking. CORRECTED- Un-dated heavy cream was voluntarily discarded.

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1. (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date. (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food. (D) Approved date marking systems. (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container. (F) Does not apply to shellstock.  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma). [Pf]

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 (A)(1) Some foods in the steam table were observed with internal temperatures below 135F and included mashed potatoes (117F), a portion of lasagna (97F-119F), and red sauce (124F). Other foods were observed with internal temperatures at 140F/above depending on when product was prepared and placed in the holding wells. Mashed potatoes were replaced with fresh product, which was observed with an internal temperature of 164F in the warmer. Lasagna was discarded as another portion of lasagna with an internal temperature of 143F was available for service. Red sauces were reheated to 165F prior to placing back in the steam table for service.
Water in the main holding well was observed at 170F, but products in the steam table were double panned. Double panning is not best practice if hot water is not adequate in the second pan to help maintain foods at 135F/above during hot holding. Kitchen manager stated he would change his process for hot holding at the steam table and monitor temperatures to verify best practice for hot holding.
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control, cooked hot foods that require time/temperature control for safety shall be maintained at 135F/above.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.citation_text:

Whipping cream was also observed without a proper date mark at the bar during the previous routine inspection. Ensure proper date marks for all prepared TCS foods.
Refrigerated, ready to eat TCS food prepared and packaged by a food processing plant shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened and if the food is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the food shall be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded, based on the temperature and time combinations specified in ¶ (A). The day the original container is opened in the food establishment shall be counted as Day 1, and the day or date marked by the food establishment may not exceed a manufacturer’s use-by date if the manufacturer determined the use-by date based on food safety.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.12 PIC was observed washing hands without proper technique. Manual faucet was shut off without a barrier. Proper handwashing technique was discussed. 
To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink.
Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying.
findings.citation_text:
2-301.13 PIC was observed going between tasks without washing hands. A wet wiping cloth from a sani-bucket on the cook line was handled to wipe the food thermometer between temperature checks. PIC did not wash hands prior to touching mushrooms that were relocated between pans on the cook line. Handwashing between tasks was discussed, and PIC was observed washing hands between tasks the remainder of inspection.,
NOTE: Placing hands in and out of sanitizer solution does not count as having clean or sanitized hands to go directly to handling food, single service articles, or clean dishes. 
--PIC was also observed wiping his hands with a wet wiping cloth from sanitizer solution while walking around the kitchen. Proper use of wiping cloths was discussed. If hands need to be wiped, then they need to be properly washed. Cease the practice of wiping hands on wiping cloths.
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. Hands must also be washed after doing anything with sanitizer or other chemicals and after engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Proper reheating procedures for hot holding
findings.citation_text:

TCS food that is cooked, cooled, and reheated for hot holding shall be reheated so that all parts of the food reach a temperature of at least 165F for 15 seconds and done rapidly to the time the food is between 41F and 165F may not exceed 2 hrs.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.12, 2-301.14, & 2-301.15 Bartender was observed rinsing hands at the prep sink by the salad cooler in the kitchen and then retrieving paper towels from the handsink by the walkin cooler to dry his hands. Bartender was advised to always use designated handsinks for handwashing and to properly wash hands when needed.
Owner wiped his hands on a dry wiping cloth between tasks while working on the cook line. Proper handwashing between tasks was discussed, and owner washed his hands at the handsink prior to continuing with preparation of a food order. 
Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying. To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink.
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. Hands must also be washed before putting on gloves/between glove changes and after engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.
Food employees shall clean their hands in a handwashing sink or approved automatic handwashing facility and may not clean their hands in a sink used for food prep, or warewashing, or in a service sink or a curbed cleaning facility used for the disposal of mop water and similar liquid waste.

findings.title: Proper cooling time and temperature
findings.citation_text:
3-501.14 Pan of alfredo sauce in the walkin cooler prepared this morning at 10am was observed with an internal temperature of 48F after 4pm. Portion in question was discarded. A smaller portion of alfredo also prepared this morning and cooled was observed at 41F. Owner noted ice baths were used prior to placing pans in the walkin cooler. Parameters for proper cooling were discussed.
Cooked time/temperature control for safety food shall be cooled within 2 hours from 135F to 70F and within an additional 4 hours from 70F to 41F/below. Foods must be cooled in a total of 6 hours from 135F to 41F/below. 
Monitor the temperature of cooling foods with clean, calibrated stem thermometers to ensure foods are reaching bench mark temperatures in the designated time frames for proper cooling.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 Bowl of salad in the chiller was observed with surface temperatures of 46F-52F and internal temperatures of 50F-52F. Product was in use since 11am and was discarded.
Sliced tomato and cut leaf lettuce on the server line held in an ice bath had internal temperatures of 60F and 55F respectively. Only the bottom of the pan was in direct contact with the ice bath. Lettuce and tomato were discarded. Whipped butter packets in a pan at the same ice bath had internal temperatures of 41F for packets in the bottom of the pan and 84F for those in the top. Butter packets were discarded. A time control policy was established for these three items during the inspection today. 
Fettuccine in the 2 door cooler had an internal temperature of 48F-50F. Owner noted it was out for ~45 minutes during lunch service. Temperature was to be monitored and noodles discarded if they did not drop to 41F/below within the hour. 
Top portion of cooked vegetables in an ice bath on the cook line had an internal temperature of 53F, while the product lower in the pan was at 41F. Owner was advised on submersion of pans in ice baths and use of less product to help maintain colder temperatures. Top layer of vegetables were removed and discarded. 
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as a public health control, cold TCS foods shall be maintained at 41F/below.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.citation_text:
3-501.17 Cooked chicken and at least one pan of noodles in the 2 door cooler did not have date marks. Also, an open gallon of milk in the walkin cooler was without a date mark. Prep/open dates were provided. Ensure proper dates are indicated on all ready to eat, refrigerated foods that require date marking. 
Refrigerated, ready to eat, time/temperature control for safety food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the food shall be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature 41F/less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation and/or the original packaging is opened shall be counted as Day 1.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.112 Heat sanitizing dish machine was not working properly. Wash temperature never went beyond 140F according to the gauge. The final rinse temperature was at 188F according to the rinse gauge, but Thermolabel heat strips verified the final rinse was not reaching 160F at the surface of the dishes. The heat strips did not turn black (4 separate strips were used at different times). A call for service was made. Until the dish machine is properly heat sanitizing, utensils and equipment need to be manually washed, rinsed, and sanitized. Dish machine may also be used for an initial wash prior to manual sanitization at the 3 part sink. 
The temperature of the fresh hot water sanitizing rinse as it enters the manifold may not be more than 194F or less than 180F for any dish machine that is not a stationary rack, single temperature machine.
findings.citation_text:
4-602.11 Can opener had buildup along the edge of the blade and metal shavings in the crevice around the blade. Can opener was left soiled from previous use and not yet used during operations today. Can opener was taken to dish area to be cleaned and sanitized.
Surfaces of utensils and equipment contacting food that is not time/temperature control for safety (TCS) shall be cleaned at any time when contamination may have occurred.
Equipment food contact surfaces and utensils used with time/temperature control for safety food shall be cleaned and sanitized throughout the day at least every 4 hours.

Stem of the food thermometer and the case had some stuck on food debris. Thermometer and case were cleaned during the inspection. Sanitizing between uses and manual wash, rinse, sanitize up to every 4 hours after continuous use were discussed. 
Food temperature measuring devices shall be cleaned before use or storage. 

Back surface of the baffle in the ice machine was soiled with mold accumulation. Owner noted the ice machine was cleaned and sanitized after the last inspection. Ice machine needs to be cleaned an sanitized as frequently as needed to eliminate buildup of mold. 
Equipment with enclosed components, such as ice machines, shall be cleaned at a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: Proper cooling time and temperature
findings.citation_text:
3-501.14 Leftover foods from the previous evening were not properly cooled. Stacked pans of lasagna, manicotti, and sausage had internal temperatures of 50F-51F. The inner surfaces of the lids had condensation buildup on them. Also, a medium sized stainless steel pan full to the top with mashed potatoes had an internal temperature of 55F. All foods leftover from the previous evening were discarded. Proper cooling was discussed. 
Cooked TCS food shall be cooled within 2 hours from 135ºF to 70°F and within an additional 4 hours from 70°F to 41°F/below. Foods must be cooled in a total of 6 hours from 135ºF to 41°F/below. Utilize one or more of the following methods based on the type of food being cooled to allow for rapid/proper cooling: (1) Placing the food in shallow pans; (2) Separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; (3) Using rapid cooling equipment; (4) Stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; (5) Using containers that facilitate heat transfer; (6) Adding ice as an ingredient; or (7) Other effective methods.

findings.title: Gloves used properly

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.citation_text:

Ice buildup on the condenser could have been causing an issue (see general comments). Salad cooler was just stocked this morning from products cold held in the walkin cooler, and the intention was to maintain foods at proper cold temperature when they were stocked. Manager was advised to use time control for the salad cooler until it could be properly defrosted. Foods would be served through lunch service and then replaced with fresh product.

Noodles, baked potatoes, and soup in the walkin cooler had internal temperatures of 47°F-50°F. Shell eggs had a surface temperature around 46°F. A huge delivery was received this morning and the cooler had to be stocked (see general comments). The air temp was blowing out below 40F. Kitchen Manager was advised to monitor temperatures to make sure they drop to 41°F/below. If products are questionable after lunch, then use or discard.

Cold foods shall be maintained at 41F/below at all times during storage, display, and service. .

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.comment:
750.510, 512, & 1120 - Cook was observed carrying a damp wiping cloth in his hands and wiping hands on the cloth after placing equipment in the dirty dish area. Cook stated the wiping cloth was not intended for his hands but was used to wipe down the counters. Wiping cloth was placed in the sanitizer solution on the cook line and hands were washed.

Member of the wait staff was observed putting on gloves and did not first wash her hands. Employee was advised on handwashing before putting on gloves.

Employees shall properly wash their hands any time hands may have been contaminated, prior to putting on gloves/between glove changes, and prior to working with food, clean equipment, and unwrapped single service articles. 
Wiping cloths are not intended for use on hands. Cease the practice of wiping hands on damp or dry wiping cloths.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored

Maintain sani-solutions prepared with the product in use at 150-400ppm quat as directed on label directions.

Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained

750.1060 - Hot water had low pressure at the back kitchen handsink adjacent to the dish area. Kitchen Manager tried adjusting the pressure with the water line shut off, but it did not appear to be changing the pressure. Call a plumber for service.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.citation_text:
750.140 - Pan of mashed potatoes in the walkin cooler had surface and internal temperatures at 80°F and 82°F-92°F respectively. Product was on a roll cart and did not have any labeling. Kitchen Manager stated the product was just prepared prior to inspector's arrival and still within the first hour of the cooling process. Mashed potatoes were placed on an ice bath to speed up the cooling process.

TCS foods shall be labeled or tagged with date and time of preparation and rapidly cooled to an internal temperature of 41°F. Monitor the time and temperature to ensure cooked foods are reaching bench mark temperatures in the designated time frame for proper cooling: 135°F to 70°F w/in 2hrs & 70°F to 41°F/below w/in an additional 4 hours. Foods prepared from ingredients starting at ambient temperature must reach 41°F/below w/in 4hrs.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.citation_text:
750.120 & 250 - Vegetable beef soup in the walkin cooler was observed with surface and internal temperatures at 50°F-51°F. Kitchen Manager noted the product was out for ~45 minutes at lunch time while product was removed to be reheated for hot holding. Container was placed on ice to help quickly drop the temperature.

Pan of vegetable soup on a roll cart was observed with surface and internal temperatures at 62°F-63°F. Kitchen Manager chose to discard the product.

Cold foods that require time/temperature control for safety (TCS) shall be maintained at 41°F/below at all times during storage, display and service. Be mindful that it doesn't take long for product temperatures to get in the danger zone above 41°F when out at ambient temperature. Promptly place foods back in coolers after retrieving the portion needed.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.citation_text:

All foods were rearranged and placed in proper storage order with ready to eat foods on the top shelf above all other products and raw fish stored above raw meats.
 
All raw meat shall be properly stored, in the order of their cooking requirements with the lowest temperatures above all other meats and those with higher required cooking temperatures stored beneath.
All food shall be stored properly in order to prevent cross-contamination.  Store ready to eat foods above or away from raw foods.

findings.comment: 750-830 The dishmachine had to complete three full cycles before reaching the desired 180F for proper heat sanitizing. Dishes were run through the machine prior to the inspection. The operator was informed of the proper temperature. It is suggested that signage be placed on the machine so staff is aware of the proper temperature. Make sure only individuals aware of how to use the machine are present. All hot water for sanitizing dishes and equipment must be a minimum of 180F when it leaves the dishwashing machine manifold in order to kill pathogens.  Properly sanitize all items. Check and maintain the dishwasher frequently.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment: 750-250 Observed shredded cheese (probed at 63F), diced tomato mixture (probed 64F), and homemade italian dressing to be held on an inoperable prep cooler over 41F. Some of the dressings within the top of this same cooler are observed under 41F because they are being stored on an ice bath. Use the ice bath throughout the top of the preparation cooler. Onions do not need to be colds held. Also, obseerved a shallow ice bath beneath wet batter for chicken. Cook stated that the bath was just created in order to quickly bread some chicken. Ice bath was limited to contact with the very bottom of the container holding the wet batter. During the inspection, items were being placed in the cooler. Discussed proper generation of an ice bath OR the use of time as control. Bringing foods from the cooler to the counter and back and forth between cooler and counter is called temperature abuse. Once an item hass been pulled from the cooler make sure the intent is known. If a portion of the food is going to be used and then placed within the cooler make sure that a proper ice bath is created to hold foods  at 41F. If the food  pulled  from the cooler will likely be used to completion then think about using time as a control. Cease temperature abuse.  All potentially hazardous foods shall be kept at 41°F or below while on display and service.
